Subject: GPU slotlineup for Nilytics pilot & weekly sync

Hi Nora + team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — excited about the Nilytics pilot. High-level ask so we can align sales/finance/infra this week:

- Pilot window: target start 2027-08-01 for a 3-month paid pilot.
- Expected workload: ~200 concurrent active users at peak, heavy batched embedding and short-gen traffic (avg seq len ~256).
- SLOs: p95 latency target ~350ms for short-gen; embeddings throughput of ~10k reqs/min.

Attached is a quick MAP spreadsheet with expected env breakdown (dev/stage/prod) and traffic assumptions. Can you confirm the split between dev/stage/prod and any hard start dates? We'll use those numbers to size dedicated slots.

Immediate asks for Redwood internal routing:
1) Finance: what reservation levels and cost tiers do you need to propose to Nilytics for a pilot (month-to-month or 3mo commit)?
2) Infra/Ops: rough ETA to reserve dedicated capacity and the minimum slot size we should propose (A100-equivalent vs smaller instances).
3) Sales: I'll own the hubspot deal and run weekly syncs. Propose Fridays 10:00am PT for 30m cadence this week.

Attachments: Nilytics_MAPlist_v1.xlsx (traffic & env assumptions)

Thanks — I'll loop in procurement once we have a concrete slot recommendation.

—Marissa

Marissa — see estimates below (very rough until infra validates exact slot mapping):

Option A — Reserved (recommended for predictability)
- 6 reserved A100-equivalent slots (balanced for embeddings + gen burst)
- Monthly cost: $78,000/mo
- One-time onboarding: $6,500 (setup, private VPC prep, access controls)
- Expected 95th pct latency: ~300–380ms depending on batch sizing

Option B — Hybrid (lower commit + burst credits)
- 3 reserved slots + burst pool up to 10 on demand
- Monthly cost (base + burst buffer): $44,000/mo (estimated)
- One-time onboarding: $6,500
- Risk: potential p95 spikes during sudden concurrent bursts; can throttle non-critical jobs to meet SLOs

Notes/asks:
- Legal/procurement will need a PO + basic SLA addendum.
- I attached a short PDF with the tier math and assumptions.

Attachment: Preliminary_Cost_Tiers.pdf

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Cloud Products, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30 10:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU slotlineup for Nilytics pilot & weekly sync

Folks — quick capacity note from infra: committed reserved pool for Aug is tight. Current constraints: two mid-sized reserved commitments already block ~40% of the A100-equivalent pool for that window.

Operationally we can do the following to hit Aug 2 with minimal impact:
1) Temporarily reassign 2 reserved slots from a low-priority trial that has flexible start (+2 slots) — frees up to 2 slots immediately.
2) Reserve 4 slots as Laura recommends (Option A reduced) and offer burst credits to cover peak spikes up to +6 additional nodes (burst governed by a token bucket).
3) If finance needs lower upfront for sales motion, use Option B and allocate 3 reserved + burst. We'll run continuous KV caching and prefer smaller batch sizes on prod to keep p95 within targets.

My recommended compromise: reserve 4 slots now, enable burst up to 8, and plan for ramp to 6 reserved after month 1 if usage justifies. That keeps risk manageable and gives Nilytics procurement a smaller initial commitment.

I'll flag infra to hold 4 slots for tentative hold until we get PO or written commitment by 2027-07-06. If we don't have a commitment by then, we'll release 2 of the tentative holds back to the pool.

—Ben
